card.name: Fancy dance
card.tagline: Athletic Native American powwow dance of Ponca origin
card.profile: Fancy dance (Fancy Feather or Fancy War Dance) is a competitive powwow dance of Native American communities, widely credited to Ponca dancer Gus McDonald, who developed it in Oklahoma in the 1920s-1930s and was the first World Champion Fancy Dancer (Wikipedia; National Cowboy & Western Heritage Museum). It arose after U.S. authorities suppressed traditional dances under the 1883 Code of Indian Offenses, when tribes created new public-friendly dances also performed at Wild West shows. It is highly athletic - spins, high kicks, leaps - with dancers in vivid regalia featuring two large feather bustles, beaded harness, roach headdress and bells; dancers must strike a pose when the drumbeat stops. Women's fancy shawl dance developed later (PowWows.com; Britannica).
card.insight: This row was mis-filed under India / South Asia: Fancy dance is NOT a South Asian dance but a Native American powwow dance, so the country is corrected to the United States (Smithsonian Center for Folklife; Oklahoma Historical Society).
